data.exact_reserve_text: This has been offset by prior accident year releases of GBP 11.5m mainly on long tail lines, recognising emerging experience as the Syndicate's live business matures.
data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate reported a prior accident year release of GBP 11.5 million, primarily from long-tail lines, reflecting favorable emerging experience as the business matures. This release occurred despite higher-than-planned catastrophe activity in 2018, including losses from Hurricane Michael, Typhoon Jebi, Camp fire, Hurricane Florence, and Typhoon Trami. The net loss ratio improved significantly, partly due to the absence of major 2017 catastrophe impacts like Hurricanes Harvey, Irma, and Maria in the current year's results.
raw_causal_phrases: prior accident year releases of GBP 11.5m mainly on long tail lines, recognising emerging experience as the Syndicate's live business matures.

Claims activity in 2018 has been impacted by catastrophe activity that was higher than planned, albeit it was the frequency of medium sized losses which did not benefit from reinsurance protection that impacted (Hurricane Michael GBP 3.5m, Typhoon Jebi GBP 2.8m, Camp fire GBP 2.8m, Hurricane Florence GBP 1.8m, Typhoon Trami GBP 1.4m).
The decrease in the net loss ratio of 60% (2017: 101%) is largely due to the impact of Hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria in 2017 (gross impact GBP 31.5m, net GBP 12.2m).
The most significant risks arise from climate changes, natural disasters and terrorist activities. For longer tail claims that take some years to settle, there is also inflation risk.
Inflation risk is mitigated by taking expected inflation into account when estimating insurance contract liabilities.

The Syndicate has also limited its exposure by imposing maximum claim amounts on certain contracts as well as the use of reinsurance arrangements in order to limit exposure to catastrophic events (e.g., hurricanes, earthquakes and flood damage).

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: The gross claims development triangle on page 15, when calculated by comparing current estimates to previous diagonals for underwriting years 2016 and older, indicates a significant strengthening of +162.88 million. This contradicts the explicit narrative statement of a GBP 11.5 million release. The narrative figure is used as it is a direct statement of prior year development. The discrepancy may be due to the partial nature of the triangle (starting from 2012) or specific accounting treatments not fully reflected in the triangle's presentation.
